Semenov et al. (2026) on dandiset 001518¶

Paper. Semenov I, Silkuniene G, Silkunas M, Pakhomova ON, Bixler JN, Ibey BL, Kochunov P, Pakhomov AG (2026). Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields. Bioelectrochemistry 171, 109283. doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2026.109283.

Dataset. DANDI:001518, version 0.261006.1957 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001518/0.261006.1957), streamed from the archive. The paper cites no version of the dataset. This is the only published version and the most recent one, so it is pinned (protocol, author step 1.3). The draft has the same 190 assets.

Claims. claims/001518/10.1016-j.bioelechem.2026.109283.yaml, written from the version of record (main text, Methods, Results, Discussion and figure legends; no supplement).

Outside input. The charging time constant of Eq. (1) is taken from reference [20] of the paper, Semenov et al. (2025), Bioelectrochemistry 168, 109143, doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2025.109143: tau = 44.5 ns/um x R, the fit through the origin in its Results. The paper says it used this fit (Methods 2.3).

Revision after verification round 1. The factor from volts to V/cm is now taken as 5.6 V/cm per volt (top, 1400 V/cm at 250 V), which agrees with the electrode geometry of Methods 2.2. The earlier choice (bottom, 1.72) was fitted to the dyes' calibration, which fig3-dye-sensitivity tests. The Di-8-ANEPPS claims at 570 V/cm and above are therefore tested. Added: a check of the automated trace with an edge-following trace as a variant, a camera-offset background reading, pole values at all 19 sets, a drift control for fig2b-di8-decline-within-set, an offset-removed variant for fig3-fluovolt-nonlinear, and every criterion over a sweep of factors (section before the summary).

Revision after verification round 2. No outcome changed. Added a fine grid of factors (1.40 to 2.30 V/cm per volt) for fig3-dye-sensitivity, and corrected the baseline range in fig2a-fluovolt-stable and the reading of the bleaching offset in fig7b-charging-during-pulse.

Data check¶

Each file is one set of 100 images. The session description gives the dye and the pulse amplitude in volts; there is no table of trials, no cell outline, no field direction and no pixel size. The checks below compare what the paper describes with the values.

The dandiset holds ten experiments from one day, five with Di-8-ANEPPS (c1 to c5) and five with FluoVolt (c7 to c11). Each is one escalation of 19 sets of 1-us pulses from 25 to 250 V, with the voltage raised set by set. The paper's escalations (Fig. 2A, 2B and 4A, 4B) have nine sets, 43 to 1400 V/cm (Fig. 2 legend: "9 cycles"), with n = 4 for FluoVolt and 5 for Di-8-ANEPPS. The files say the electrodes are 1.00 mm apart; the paper says 1.6 mm. Nothing in the files records the alternating protocol (Fig. 2C, D), 0.3-us pulses (Fig. 4D), Gd3+ (Fig. 5), Fluo-4 Ca2+ imaging (Fig. 6) or the two-pulse protocol (Fig. 7).

The voltages span a factor of 10, while the paper's field strengths span a factor of 1400 / 43 = 33. Field strength is proportional to voltage (Methods 2.2), so no single factor maps all nine of the paper's levels onto these sets. The factor from volts to V/cm is in neither the paper, its reference [20], nor the files. Two endpoint readings are run: top puts the paper's highest level on the highest voltage (1400 V/cm at 250 V, 5.6 V/cm per V), and bottom puts its lowest on the lowest (43 V/cm at 25 V, 1.72 V/cm per V). The data check below weighs them.

Frame 0 of almost every set, and a few other frames, are dark: their mean is near the camera offset, so the laser did not fire. They are left out (helper, good_frames); with frame 0 out, the baseline has 39 images in most sets, not the paper's 40. The cell-free background is about 330 counts, a large part of the membrane signal, so background subtraction about doubles dF (ranges printed below); both readings are run where the claims file names them.

Every field of view holds several cells (3 to 6 found), while the paper analysed one cell per experiment and does not say which. The cell analysed in each experiment cannot be identified from the files. Three readings are run: (i) the mean of the experiment's responding cells, with the experiment as the unit (n = 5 per dye); (ii) the responding cell nearest the image centre, one per experiment; (iii) every responding cell as a unit. The field direction, which the files do not record, is found from the data: in every experiment the side whose emission rises (the cathode-facing side, Methods 2.3) lies between 94 and 106 degrees of the image's +x axis, that is towards the bottom of the image. With a 16-um camera pixel and the 60x objective, the mean radius is about 6.7 um. The paper gives about 8 um for CHO cells as a typical value, so the pixel size is consistent with the data but not shown by them.

No two sets share their frame-by-frame laser fluctuation or a cell profile, so no recording is deposited twice. The cells of each experiment are linked from set to set by position (within 10 pixels); the same object is found in all 19 sets, so a cell is treated as the same across the sets of an experiment.

In [8]:
# Shared clock: the pulse starts at image 41 (index 40) in every set (Methods 2.3: 40 baseline
# images, then 60 with the pulse). Polarization (cathodic minus anodic dF, halved) in 10-image
# windows either side of a boundary; the step should be largest at the true onset, and absent at
# the same boundary in the lowest-voltage sets if the response is a response.
def polarization_frames(df):
    return np.stack([(a - b) / 2 for a, b in zip(df.frames_cath, df.frames_anod)])

onsets, steps = [], []
for (sub, volt), g in D.groupby(["subject", "volt"]):
    pol = np.nanmean(polarization_frames(g), 0)
    st = {b: np.nanmean(pol[b:b + 10]) - np.nanmean(pol[b - 10:b]) for b in range(15, 86)}
    onsets.append(dict(subject=sub, volt=volt, onset=max(st, key=lambda b: abs(st[b])), step40=st[40],
                       step30=st[30], step50=st[50]))
on = pd.DataFrame(onsets)
print("Boundary with the largest polarization step, sets at 50 V and above:")
print(on[on.volt >= 50].onset.value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
print("\nMean step (% dF) at boundaries 30, 40, 50, by voltage group:")
print(on.assign(group=pd.cut(on.volt, [0, 25, 60, 120, 250])).groupby("group", observed=True)[["step30", "step40", "step50"]].mean().round(2))

In every set at 50 V and above, the polarization step is largest at index 40 or within a frame or two of it, and it grows with voltage; at boundaries 30 and 50 the step is near zero. The images are therefore on the clock the paper describes: 40 images without the pulse, then 60 with it. Because there is one stream per file, no other stream needs aligning.

In [9]:
# Field strength per volt implied by the low-field response under the paper's calibration
# (Fig. 3: 26 and 9.1% dF per 100 mV) and Eq. (1). Per cell, the slope of the half-difference
# between the poles (which cancels the uniform bleaching offset) over the sets at 25 to 60 V.
rows = []
for (dye, sub, cell), g in D.groupby(["dye", "subject", "cell"]):
    g = g[g.volt <= 60]
    half = (g.dF_cath - g.dF_anod) / 2
    slope = np.sum(half * g.volt) / np.sum(g.volt ** 2)
    R = g.R_area_um.mean()
    rows.append(dict(dye=dye, subject=sub, cell=cell, k=slope / (pef.SENS[dye] / 100 * pef.impc_mV(1.0, R, 0))))
kk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Implied V/cm per volt, per cell, if the paper's dye sensitivities hold:")
print(kk.groupby("dye").k.describe().round(2))
print("\nField at the midpoint between two 0.5-mm rods (two-dimensional, helper rod_field_per_volt), V/cm per volt:")

Two checks bear on the factor, and they point in different directions.

  • If the paper's dye sensitivities hold, the low-field response implies a median of 1.5 to 1.6 V/cm per volt in each dye, near bottom (1.72). This uses the sensitivities that fig3-dye-sensitivity tests, so a factor chosen this way cannot be used to test them.
  • The electrode geometry of Methods 2.2 (rods 0.5 mm in diameter, 1.6 mm apart) gives 4.64 to 7.19 V/cm per volt at the midpoint in a two-dimensional model, depending on whether 1.6 mm is the gap or the centre distance. The files' 1.00 mm gives 8.02 to 17.54. top (5.6) lies in the range for the paper's geometry; bottom is 2.7 to 10 times below every geometric value.

The top reading is adopted as an assumption. It is the one the geometry supports, it does not use any quantity a claim tests, and it puts the dataset's highest amplitude on the paper's highest field. The two-dimensional model ignores the dish bottom and the rod ends, so it gives the order of the factor, not its value. bottom is shown as a variant, and every criterion is run over factors from 1.5 to 8 in the section before the summary. Under top the sets cover 140 to 1400 V/cm, so the paper's 43 V/cm level has no set. At 25 V the mean of the two poles is -3.9% (Di-8-ANEPPS) and -2.1% (FluoVolt). This uniform offset matches the bleaching the paper reports in its own Di-8-ANEPPS dF at 43 V/cm (Results 3.2, paragraph 3: about 5% added at the anodic pole and removed at the cathodic pole).

# Pole dF against voltage, mean of experiment means (reading i), both dyes.
def units(df, reading):
    # (i) experiment mean of its cells; (ii) the cell nearest the image centre; (iii) every cell.
    if reading == "experiment":
        g = df.groupby(["dye", "subject", "volt"], as_index=False)
        out = g.mean(numeric_only=True)
        out["unit"] = out.subject
        return out
    if reading == "centre":
        pick = df.groupby("subject").apply(lambda g: g.loc[g.dist_centre_px.idxmin(), "cell"])
        out = df[df.cell == df.subject.map(pick)].copy()
        out["unit"] = out.subject
        return out
    out = df.copy()
    out["unit"] = out.subject + "/" + out.cell.astype(str)
    return out

READINGS = ["experiment", "centre", "cells"]
K = dict(pef.FIELD_PER_VOLT)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.6), sharey=True)
for ax, dye in zip(axes, ["FV", "Di8"]):
    u = units(D[D.dye == dye], "experiment")
    for pole, col in [("cathodic", "dF_cath"), ("anodic", "dF_anod")]:
        m = u.groupby("volt")[col].agg(["mean", "sem"])
        ax.errorbar(m.index, m["mean"], m["sem"], marker="o", ms=3, label=pole)
    ax.set_title({"FV": "FluoVolt", "Di8": "Di-8-ANEPPS"}[dye] + " (n = 5 experiments)")
    ax.set_xlabel("pulse amplitude (V)")
    sec = ax.secondary_xaxis("top", functions=(lambda v: v * K["top"], lambda e: e / K["top"]))
    sec.set_xlabel("V/cm, top reading (adopted)")
    ax.axhline(0, color="0.7", lw=0.5)
axes[0].set_ylabel("collapsed pole dF (%)")
axes[0].legend()

Check of the automated membrane trace¶

The pole dF magnitudes below are about half the paper's at most levels, so the trace is checked on the 120 V and 250 V sets of every experiment (re-read from the archive): the background-subtracted pole dF on 1-pixel rings from 8 pixels inside to 8 outside the trace. The 6-pixel trace spans offsets -2.5 to +2.5. If the trace sat off the membrane, the pole dF would rise when the ring moves onto it.

In [12]:
def radial_one(job):
    sub, volt = job
    ss, keep, cath, _ = resp[sub]
    j = [s["volt"] for s in ss].index(volt)
    return sub, volt, ss[j], [row[j] for row in keep], pef.radial_poles(ss[j], [row[j] for row in keep], cath)

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(10) as ex:
    radial = list(ex.map(radial_one, [(sub, v) for sub in sorted(resp) for v in (120, 250)]))
rows = []
for sub, volt, s, cis, r in radial:
    off = r["offsets"]
    for k, c in enumerate(cis):
        tr = D[(D.subject == sub) & (D.volt == volt) & (D.cell == k)].iloc[0]
        for pole in ("cath", "anod"):
            v = r["cells"][k][pole]
            sign = 1 if pole == "cath" else -1
            band = np.abs(off) <= 3
            rows.append(dict(dye=s["dye"], subject=sub, volt=volt, cell=k, pole=pole, trace=tr[f"dF_{pole}"],
                             ring0=v[off == 0][0], best_in_band=sign * np.max(sign * v[band]),
                             best_offset_in_band=int(off[band][np.argmax(sign * v[band])]),
                             best_8px=sign * np.max(sign * v), best_offset_8px=int(off[np.argmax(sign * v)])))
rc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Pole dF (%): the trace, the ring on the trace, and the largest |dF| over rings within 3 and 8 pixels;"
      " mean over experiments of the experiment means:")
print(rc.groupby(["dye", "volt", "subject", "pole"])[["trace", "ring0", "best_in_band", "best_8px"]].mean()
      .groupby(["dye", "volt", "pole"]).mean().round(1).to_string())
print("\nLargest single-cell values, rings within 3 pixels:")
print(rc.groupby(["dye", "pole"]).best_in_band.agg(["min", "max"]).round(1).to_string())
print("\nOffset (pixels) of the largest |dF| within 8 pixels, counts:", rc.best_offset_8px.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())
print("Dark-frame level of these sets (camera offset):", f"{np.nanmin([x[4]['dark'] for x in radial]):.0f} to {np.nanmax([x[4]['dark'] for x in radial]):.0f} counts")

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 5, figsize=(15, 6.4))
for ax, (sub, volt, s, cis, r) in zip(axes.ravel(), [x for x in radial if x[1] == 250]):

On the ring at the trace, experiment-mean pole dF is within 3 points of the trace value. The largest |dF| over rings within 3 pixels of the trace is 5.5 to 7.7 points larger (it picks the largest of seven noisy values, so it is biased upwards). For FluoVolt it reaches 43.4% and -57.1% at the most, against the paper's 66% and -83%. For Di-8-ANEPPS it reaches 30.9% and -35.0%, against 57% and -55%. Rings up to 8 pixels outside give larger values, because there F0 approaches the background. They stay below the paper's FluoVolt values (50.9%, -65.0%) and its Di-8-ANEPPS cathodic value (36.7%); the Di-8-ANEPPS anodic value reaches -55.3% at 250 V. Single cells reach 79.5% and -105.5% (FluoVolt) and 53.7% and -84.4% (Di-8-ANEPPS) within 3 pixels, so the paper's values lie inside the spread of single cells. A misplaced trace does not explain the shortfall of the means.

The overlay shows two faults of the peak trace (red). In some cells it is drawn inwards, where bright spots inside the cell outshine the rim. In c7 two touching cells are found as one object. A second trace that follows the cell edge (cyan; helper trace_edge) is run as a variant. It follows most outlines, but bridges into a touching neighbour in a few cells. With it the largest experiment-mean pole values over the 19 sets are 26.9% and -41.3% (FluoVolt) and 25.1% and -30.4% (Di-8-ANEPPS), no nearer the paper's. Its mean radius is 9.90 um, against 6.72 um for the peak trace. The sweep before the summary runs every criterion with both traces.

fig3-dye-sensitivity¶

Fitted linearly through the origin over -150 to +150 mV IMPC, FluoVolt changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.

Every perimeter point of every analysed cell, in the sets from 43 to 360 V/cm, against IMPC from Eq. (1) with the cell's own radius and tau = 44.5 ns/um x R (reference [20]). Least squares through the origin over IMPC from -150 to +150 mV. Readings run: field mapping (top, adopted; bottom), background (b subtracted, a none), radius (equal-area, perimeter / 2 pi), cells (all responding cells, or the cell nearest the image centre), and sets (every set up to 360 V/cm, or only the sets nearest the paper's levels 43, 150, 230 and 360 V/cm). The correlation coefficient is read as (a) Pearson r and (b) the square root of the uncentred R2.

def calib_points(dye, mapping, background, radius, cells, which_sets, detrend=False):
    df = (D if background else D_raw)
    df = df[df.dye == dye]
    if cells == "centre":
        df = units(df, "centre")
    k = K[mapping]
    if which_sets == "levels":
        lv = pef.nearest_sets(df.volt, k)
        df = df[df.volt.isin([v for L, v in lv.items() if L <= 360])]
    else:
        df = df[df.volt * k <= 360]
    th = np.arange(360)
    X = np.concatenate([pef.impc_mV(v * k, r, th) for v, r in zip(df.volt, df[f"R_{radius}_um"])])
    # detrend: remove each profile's mean, the uniform (bleaching) offset; a variant.
    Y = np.concatenate([p - p.mean() if detrend else p for p in df.profile.values])
    return X, Y, df

def fit0(X, Y, lim=150):
    m = np.abs(X) <= lim
    x, y = X[m], Y[m]
    if len(x) == 0:
        return dict(slope=np.nan, r_pearson=np.nan, r_uncentred=np.nan, n_points=0)
    return dict(slope=100 * np.sum(x * y) / np.sum(x * x), r_pearson=np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1],
                r_uncentred=np.sum(x * y) / np.sqrt(np.sum(x * x) * np.sum(y * y)), n_points=int(m.sum()))

EXP3 = {"FV": (26, 2.6, 0.96, 0.096), "Di8": (9.1, 0.91, 0.78, 0.078)}

def fig3_row(mapping, background=True, radius="area", cells="all", which="all"):
    out = dict(mapping=mapping, bg="b" if background else "a", radius=radius, cells=cells, sets=which)
    ok = True
    for dye in ["FV", "Di8"]:
        X, Y, df = calib_points(dye, mapping, background, radius, cells, which)
        f = fit0(X, Y)
        s0, ts, r0, tr = EXP3[dye]
        out.update({f"{dye}_slope": f["slope"], f"{dye}_r_pearson": f["r_pearson"], f"{dye}_r_uncentred": f["r_uncentred"],
                    f"{dye}_n_sets": df.volt.nunique(), f"{dye}_n_cells": df.groupby(["subject", "cell"]).ngroups,
                    f"{dye}_n_points": f["n_points"]})
        ok &= bool(abs(f["slope"] - s0) <= ts and (abs(f["r_pearson"] - r0) <= tr or abs(f["r_uncentred"] - r0) <= tr))
    out["reproduced"] = ok if out["FV_n_points"] and out["Di8_n_points"] else None
    return out

cal = pd.DataFrame([fig3_row(mapping, background, radius, cells, which)
                    for mapping in ["top", "bottom"] for background in [True, False] for radius in ["area", "perim"]
                    for cells in ["all", "centre"] for which in ["all", "levels"]])
print(cal.round(3).to_string(index=False))

# A reading reproduces when, for both dyes, the slope is within tolerance and r is within
# tolerance under (a) or (b).
print("Readings where both dyes meet the criterion:", int((cal.reproduced == True).sum()), "of", len(cal))
for mapping in ["top", "bottom"]:
    s = cal[cal.mapping == mapping]
    print(f"{mapping}: FluoVolt slope {s.FV_slope.min():.2f} to {s.FV_slope.max():.2f}, Di-8-ANEPPS {s.Di8_slope.min():.2f} to {s.Di8_slope.max():.2f};"
          f" r (Pearson) FluoVolt {s.FV_r_pearson.min():.3f} to {s.FV_r_pearson.max():.3f}, Di-8-ANEPPS {s.Di8_r_pearson.min():.3f} to {s.Di8_r_pearson.max():.3f}")
main = cal[(cal.mapping == "top") & (cal.bg == "b") & (cal.radius == "area") & (cal.cells == "all") & (cal.sets == "all")]
print("\nAdopted reading (top, background subtracted, equal-area radius, all cells, all sets):")
print(main.round(3).T.to_string())
by_exp = []
for dye in ["FV", "Di8"]:
    X, Y, df = calib_points(dye, "top", True, "area", "all", "all")
    sub = np.repeat(df.subject.values, 360)
    for s in np.unique(sub):
        by_exp.append(dict(dye=dye, subject=s, **fit0(X[sub == s], Y[sub == s])))
print("\nBy experiment, adopted reading:")
print(pd.DataFrame(by_exp).round(3).to_string(index=False))
# Adopted reading on a fine grid of factors around those that give the paper's slopes. The slope
# does not scale as 1 / factor, because the sets at or below 360 V/cm change with the factor.
fine = []
for k in np.round(np.arange(1.40, 2.301, 0.02), 2):
    K[f"fine{k:g}"] = k
    r = fig3_row(f"fine{k:g}")
    fine.append(dict(factor=k, sets_FV=r["FV_n_sets"], FV_slope=r["FV_slope"], FV_r=r["FV_r_pearson"],
                     FV_r_unc=r["FV_r_uncentred"], Di8_slope=r["Di8_slope"], Di8_r=r["Di8_r_pearson"],
                     Di8_r_unc=r["Di8_r_uncentred"], reproduced=r["reproduced"]))
fine = pd.DataFrame(fine)
print("\nAdopted reading over factors 1.40 to 2.30 V/cm per volt:")
print(fine.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for dye in ["FV", "Di8"]:
    s0, ts = EXP3[dye][:2]
    ok = fine.factor[(fine[f"{dye}_slope"] - s0).abs() <= ts]
    print(f"{dye}: slope within {s0} +- {ts} at factors {list(ok)}")
print("Factors on this grid that meet the criterion for both dyes:", list(fine.factor[fine.reproduced == True]))

Result: not reproduced (under the assumed factor). Under the adopted reading (top mapping, background subtracted, equal-area radius, all responding cells, the four sets from 140 to 336 V/cm), FluoVolt gives 6.10% dF per 100 mV (expected 26 +- 2.6) with r = 0.775 (Pearson) and 0.743 (uncentred), against 0.96 +- 0.096. Di-8-ANEPPS gives 2.37% (expected 9.1 +- 0.91) with r = 0.481 and 0.402, against 0.78 +- 0.078. Over the 16 top-mapping readings the slopes are 2.72 to 6.10 and 0.83 to 2.37, and by experiment 5.36 to 6.64 and 2.20 to 2.53. The slope falls as the factor rises, but not as one over the factor, because the sets at or below 360 V/cm change with it. On the grid from 1.40 to 2.30 V/cm per volt, the FluoVolt slope is within tolerance at 1.40 to 1.76 and the Di-8-ANEPPS slope at 1.82 to 2.16, and r is within tolerance for both dyes at every factor (FluoVolt 0.90 to 0.92, Di-8-ANEPPS 0.79 to 0.84). No factor on that grid or in the sweep from 1.5 to 8 meets the criterion for both dyes, so the result is not reproduced at the factors run. The factors that match each of the paper's slopes, about 1.4 to 2.2, are near the 1.5 to 1.6 that the low-field response implies under the paper's calibration (data check) and below the 4.64 to 7.19 of the electrode geometry. Under the bottom variant, which was set from this response, the slopes are 23.98 and 10.52 and r is 0.908 and 0.824. None of the 32 readings meets the criterion for both dyes. At the geometric factors (4.64 to 7.19) the slopes are 4.4 to 8.0 and 1.6 to 3.2. With the edge trace (data check) they are 4.5 and 1.8 at the adopted factor.

fig3-fluovolt-nonlinear¶

FluoVolt departed from linearity from about +-200 mV IMPC, while Di-8-ANEPPS stayed nearly linear from -500 to +500 mV; so FluoVolt's early departure reflects its dynamic range, not electroporation.

The points and line of fig3-dye-sensitivity (adopted reading; the bottom mapping as a variant). Smooths: LOWESS with span (a) 0.3, (b) 0.5, (c) 0.75, and (d) means in 50-mV bins. A departure is the smooth lying closer to zero than the line by more than 10% of the line's value. Checked on a 10-mV grid; LOWESS is evaluated with delta set to 1% of the IMPC range, which interpolates between nearby fitted points (a standard speed-up that cannot change the outcome).

The fit is through the origin, so a uniform offset of the profile (the bleaching seen at 25 V, data check) moves the smooth off the line near zero. The paper reports that bleaching in its own Di-8-ANEPPS dF (Results 3.2, paragraph 3) and does not say it removed it, so the main reading keeps it. As a variant, each profile's mean over the 360 points (the uniform offset; the cosine averages to zero) is removed before the fit and the smooth (detrend).

def smooth(X, Y, how):
    o = np.argsort(X)
    X, Y = X[o], Y[o]
    if how == "bins":
        edges = np.arange(np.floor(X.min() / 50) * 50, X.max() + 50, 50)
        idx = np.digitize(X, edges)
        xs = np.array([X[idx == i].mean() for i in np.unique(idx) if (idx == i).sum() >= 20])
        ys = np.array([Y[idx == i].mean() for i in np.unique(idx) if (idx == i).sum() >= 20])
        return xs, ys
    fr = lowess(Y, X, frac=how, it=0, delta=0.01 * (X.max() - X.min()), return_sorted=True)
    return fr[:, 0], fr[:, 1]

def departure(X, Y, slope, how):
    xs, ys = smooth(X, Y, how)
    grid = np.arange(np.ceil(xs.min() / 10) * 10, xs.max(), 10)
    sm = np.interp(grid, xs, ys)
    line = slope / 100 * grid
    dep = (np.abs(line) - np.sign(line) * sm) > 0.1 * np.abs(line)
    dep[grid == 0] = False
    return grid, sm, line, dep

def nonlinear_rows(mapping, detrend=False, smooths=(0.3, 0.5, 0.75, "bins")):
    res, cur = [], {}
    for dye in ["FV", "Di8"]:
        X, Y, _ = calib_points(dye, mapping, True, "area", "all", "all", detrend=detrend)
        slope = fit0(X, Y)["slope"]
        for how in smooths:
            grid, sm, line, dep = departure(X, Y, slope, how)
            cur[(mapping, detrend, dye, how)] = (grid, sm, line, dep)
            r = dict(mapping=mapping, detrend=detrend, dye=dye, smooth=how, slope=slope, data_range=f"{grid.min():.0f} to {grid.max():.0f}")
            if dye == "FV":
                hi = np.abs(grid) >= 220
                both = (grid >= 220).any() and (grid <= -220).any()
                r.update(grid_pts_220_to_end=int(hi.sum()), ok=bool(both and dep[hi].all()), departing_pts=int(dep[hi].sum()))
            else:
                inr = np.abs(grid) <= 500
                r.update(grid_pts_in_range=int(inr.sum()), ok=not bool(dep[inr].any()), departing_pts=int(dep[inr].sum()),
                         departing_at=", ".join(f"{g:.0f}" for g in grid[inr & dep][:12]))
            res.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(res), cur

def nonlinear_verdict(t):
    # Reproduced when every smooth gives FluoVolt departing and Di-8-ANEPPS not departing.
    return bool(t.ok.all())

t0 = time.time()
nl, curves = [], {}
for mapping in ["top", "bottom"]:
    for detrend in [False, True]:
        t, c = nonlinear_rows(mapping, detrend)
        nl.append(t)
        curves.update(c)
nl = pd.concat(nl)
print(nl.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("\nReproduced (every smooth), by mapping and offset removal:")
print(nl.groupby(["mapping", "detrend"]).apply(nonlinear_verdict).to_string())
print(f"({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)")

Result: not reproduced (under the assumed factor). Under the top mapping the FluoVolt smooth does not depart from the line at |IMPC| of 220 mV and above under any LOWESS span (0 departing grid points of 48), and in 12 of 42 points with 50-mV bins. It lies above the line: 107 to 113% of the line at +220 mV and 128 to 134% at -220 mV. Di-8-ANEPPS departs at 22 to 23 grid points under every smooth, on the positive side near zero, where its smooth is -27 to 0.5% of the line at +100 mV. With each profile's offset removed, FluoVolt still does not depart, and Di-8-ANEPPS departs under span 0.3 and bins (2 and 6 points) but not under 0.5 and 0.75. So no reading meets the criterion. Under the bottom variant FluoVolt departs at every point from 220 mV under every smooth, but Di-8-ANEPPS departs at 58 to 64 points (40 to 50 with the offset removed), so the criterion fails there as well. No factor in the sweep meets it.

fig2a-fluovolt-saturation¶

With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.

Per-image pole dF (the Fig. 2 measure, Methods 2.3), averaged over the 60 pulse images of each set, per cell, then across units. The paper's levels are the sets nearest them (helper, nearest_sets, within 15%). Both mappings, three cell readings, and three background readings are run: (b) the cell-free median (adopted), (a) none, and the camera offset alone (the dark-frame level), a variant.

def verdict(*conds):
    # Combine conditions: False if any fails, None (untestable) if any is missing, else True.
    if any(c is False for c in conds):
        return False
    if any(c is None for c in conds):
        return None
    return True

def level_table(df, mapping, cols, reading):
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(df.volt, K[mapping])
    u = units(df, reading)
    out = {}
    for L, v in lv.items():
        g = u[u.volt == v]
        out[L] = {c: (g[c].mean(), g[c].sem(), len(g)) for c in cols}
    return out, lv

def show_levels(dye, cols, background=True, readings=READINGS, mappings=("top", "bottom")):
    df = {True: D, False: D_raw, "offset": D_off}[background]
    df = df[df.dye == dye]
    rows = []
    for mapping in mappings:
        for reading in readings:
            tab, lv = level_table(df, mapping, cols, reading)
            for L, d in tab.items():
                r = dict(mapping=mapping, cells=reading, level=L, volt=lv[L], n=d[cols[0]][2])
                for c in cols:
                    r[c] = round(d[c][0], 1)
                    r[c + "_se"] = round(d[c][1], 1)
                rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def check_fig2a(t):
    t = t.set_index("level")
    c360 = t.pi_cath.get(360, np.nan)
    a570 = t.pi_anod.get(570, np.nan)
    hi = [L for L in (1000, 1200, 1400) if L in t.index]
    out = dict(cath_360=c360, cath_360_ok=bool(abs(c360 - 66) <= 6.6) if not np.isnan(c360) else None, anod_570=a570,
               anod_570_ok=bool(abs(a570 - (-83)) <= 8.3) if not np.isnan(a570) else None,
               cath_360_is_max=bool(c360 >= t.pi_cath.max()) if not np.isnan(c360) else None,
               max_cath=t.pi_cath.max(), max_cath_level=int(t.pi_cath.idxmax()),
               min_anod=t.pi_anod.min(), min_anod_level=int(t.pi_anod.idxmin()), levels_1000_1400=len(hi))
    out["anod_not_more_neg"] = bool(all(t.pi_anod[L] >= a570 - 8.3 for L in (780, 1000, 1200, 1400) if L in t.index)) if hi and not np.isnan(a570) else None
    out["cath_hi_below_360"] = bool(all(t.pi_cath[L] < c360 for L in hi)) if hi and not np.isnan(c360) else None
    out["reproduced"] = verdict(out["cath_360_ok"], out["anod_570_ok"], out["cath_360_is_max"], out["anod_not_more_neg"], out["cath_hi_below_360"])
    return out

def fig2a_sat(mapping, reading="experiment", background=True):
    t = show_levels("FV", ["pi_cath", "pi_anod"], background, readings=[reading], mappings=[mapping])
    return check_fig2a(t)

Largest per-experiment cathodic value at any set: 43.6%; most negative anodic: -61.1%

Result: not reproduced. At 360 V/cm (60 V under the top mapping) the per-image cathodic dF is 23.5% (experiment means; 20.1 for the cell nearest the centre, 24.1 over all cells), against 66 +- 6.6. At 570 V/cm the anodic dF is -35.8% (-33.7 and -38.6), against -83 +- 8.3. The cathodic maximum is 35.9% at 570 V/cm, not at 360. Over all 19 sets the largest experiment-mean cathodic value is 36.1% and the most negative anodic value -49.5%. Per experiment the values reach 43.6% and -61.1% at most. With the camera offset as background they are 17.3% and -25.2%, and without background 12.1% and -17.9%. The magnitudes fail under every mapping, cell and background reading and every factor in the sweep. Under the top mapping the cathodic response falls from 35.9% at 570 V/cm to 21.2% at 1400 V/cm and the anodic one grows from -35.8% to -49.4%.

fig2a-fluovolt-stable¶

FluoVolt measurements were stable without pulses (no significant bleaching or photosensitization), and the response within each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses, even at 1000 V/cm and above.

Per set and pole, the start and end of the 40 baseline images, and of the 60 pulse images, compared by a 2-tailed paired t-test over units at p < 0.05. Start and end are (a) the first and the last lit image, (b) the first 10 and the last 10. The sets are those nearest the paper's levels (main), with all 19 sets as a variant.

In [20]:
def start_end(frames, lo, hi, mode):
    seg = frames[lo:hi]
    ok = np.nonzero(~np.isnan(seg))[0]
    if mode == "a":
        return seg[ok[0]], seg[ok[-1]]
    return np.nanmean(seg[:10]), np.nanmean(seg[-10:])

def stability(dye, phase, mapping, reading, mode, sets_sel="levels", background=True):
    df = (D if background else D_raw)
    df = df[df.dye == dye].copy()
    lo, hi = (0, pef.N_BASE) if phase == "baseline" else (pef.N_BASE, 100)
    for pole in ["cath", "anod"]:
        se = np.array([start_end(f, lo, hi, mode) for f in df[f"frames_{pole}"]])
        df[f"s_{pole}"], df[f"e_{pole}"] = se[:, 0], se[:, 1]
    u = units(df, reading)
    if sets_sel == "levels":
        lv = pef.nearest_sets(df.volt, K[mapping])
        pick = {v: L for L, v in lv.items()}
    else:
        pick = {v: round(v * K[mapping]) for v in sorted(df.volt.unique())}
    rows = []
    for v, L in pick.items():
        g = u[u.volt == v]
        for pole in ["cath", "anod"]:
            t, p = stats.ttest_rel(g[f"s_{pole}"], g[f"e_{pole}"])
            rows.append(dict(level=L, volt=v, pole=pole, n=len(g), start=g[f"s_{pole}"].mean(), end=g[f"e_{pole}"].mean(),
                             change=(g[f"e_{pole}"] - g[f"s_{pole}"]).mean(), p=p))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def fig2a_stable(mapping, reading="experiment", mode="b", sets_sel="levels"):
    b = stability("FV", "baseline", mapping, reading, mode, sets_sel)
    q = stability("FV", "pulse", mapping, reading, mode, sets_sel)
    qh = q[q.level >= 1000]
    out = dict(baseline_tests=len(b), baseline_sig=int((b.p < 0.05).sum()), baseline_max_abs_change=b.change.abs().max(),
               pulse_1000plus_tests=len(qh), pulse_1000plus_sig=int((qh.p < 0.05).sum()),
               pulse_1000plus_max_abs_change=qh.change.abs().max() if len(qh) else np.nan)
    out["reproduced"] = verdict(out["baseline_sig"] == 0, (out["pulse_1000plus_sig"] == 0) if len(qh) else None)
    return out

sm = pd.DataFrame([dict(mapping=mapping, cells=reading, start_end=mode, sets=sets_sel, **fig2a_stable(mapping, reading, mode, sets_sel))
                   for mapping in ["top", "bottom"] for reading in READINGS for mode in ["a", "b"] for sets_sel in ["levels", "all"]])
print(sm.round(2).to_string(index=False))

All 19 sets, baseline, experiment means, 10-image windows: 4 of 38 tests at p < 0.05 (about 1.9 expected by chance); changes -3.34 to 0.64%, 32 of 38 negative

Result: not reproduced (under the assumed factor). In the baseline images (top mapping, experiment means, sets at the paper's levels, 10-image windows), the cathodic pole changes by -3.34% at 780 V/cm (2-tailed paired t-test p = 0.018, n = 5) and by -2.82% at 1000 V/cm (p = 0.003). The other 14 baseline changes lie between -3.04% and +0.64% with p from 0.055 to 0.93. Across readings, 1 to 4 of 16 baseline tests at the paper's levels and 4 to 9 of 38 over all 19 sets are significant. With experiment means over all sets, 4 of 38 are, about 1.9 being expected by chance, and 32 of 38 changes are negative (-3.34 to +0.64%), a small bleaching drift. In the pulse images at 1000 to 1400 V/cm none of the 6 tests differs with experiment means (changes -0.78 to -2.01%, p 0.09 to 0.54), and 0 or 1 of 6 under the other readings. The criterion counts any significant baseline change. In the sweep it is met only at 3.5 V/cm per volt.

fig4a-fluovolt-limits¶

FluoVolt measured and calculated IMP matched only at 43 and 150 V/cm; with stronger 1-us pulses the pole dF peaked at 71 +- 10% (cathodic) and -83.5 +- 5% (anodic), about +260 and -330 mV.

Collapsed pole dF per cell and level, mean across units; the maximum is the largest mean |dF| over the levels at each pole. Measured IMP (dF / 26 x 100 mV) against the cell's pole IMPC by 2-tailed paired and unpaired t-tests at p < 0.05.

In [22]:
def imp_vs_impc(dye, mapping, reading, background=True):
    df = (D if background else D_raw)
    df = df[df.dye == dye].copy()
    k = K[mapping]
    df["imp_cath"] = df.dF_cath / pef.SENS[dye] * 100
    df["imp_anod"] = df.dF_anod / pef.SENS[dye] * 100
    df["impc_cath"] = pef.impc_mV(df.volt * k, df.R_area_um, 0)
    df["impc_anod"] = -df.impc_cath
    u = units(df, reading)
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(df.volt, k)
    rows = []
    for L, v in lv.items():
        g = u[u.volt == v]
        for pole in ["cath", "anod"]:
            meas, calc = g[f"imp_{pole}"], g[f"impc_{pole}"]
            rows.append(dict(level=L, volt=v, pole=pole, n=len(g), dF=g[f"dF_{pole}"].mean(), dF_se=g[f"dF_{pole}"].sem(),
                             imp=meas.mean(), impc=calc.mean(), ratio=meas.mean() / calc.mean(),
                             p_paired=stats.ttest_rel(meas, calc).pvalue, p_unpaired=stats.ttest_ind(meas, calc).pvalue))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def limits_check(t, dye, exp_c, tol_c, exp_a, tol_a):
    c = t[t.pole == "cath"].set_index("level")
    a = t[t.pole == "anod"].set_index("level")
    return dict(max_cath=c.dF.max(), at=int(c.dF.idxmax()), max_cath_ok=bool(abs(c.dF.max() - exp_c) <= tol_c),
                min_anod=a.dF.min(), at_a=int(a.dF.idxmin()), min_anod_ok=bool(abs(a.dF.min() - exp_a) <= tol_a))

def fig4a_limits(mapping, reading="experiment", tests=("p_paired", "p_unpaired")):
    t = imp_vs_impc("FV", mapping, reading)
    r = limits_check(t, "FV", 71, 10, -83.5, 5)
    for test in tests:
        low = t[t.level.isin([43, 150])]
        high = t[t.level >= 230]
        r[f"{test}_no_diff_43_150"] = bool((low[test] >= 0.05).all()) if len(low) else None
        below = high.assign(b=(high[test] < 0.05) & (high.imp.abs() < high.impc.abs()))
        r[f"{test}_below_each_230plus"] = bool(below.groupby("level").b.any().all()) if len(high) else None
        r[f"reproduced_{test}"] = verdict(r["max_cath_ok"], r["min_anod_ok"], r[f"{test}_no_diff_43_150"], r[f"{test}_below_each_230plus"])
    return r

Result: not reproduced. Under the top mapping the largest mean cathodic dF is 35.9% (at 570 V/cm; 34.4 and 35.7 under the other cell readings), against 71 +- 10, and the most negative anodic value is -49.5% (1200 V/cm; -49.9 and -51.1), against -83.5 +- 5. Under the bottom variant they are 31.7 to 35.8% and -48.8 to -51.1%, and no factor in the sweep meets them. Under the top mapping there is no 43 V/cm set; at 150 V/cm measured IMP is already below IMPC (ratios 0.10 cathodic and 0.20 anodic, paired p < 0.001 and 0.001), so the match there fails. Measured IMP is below IMPC at every level from 230 V/cm (ratios 0.06 to 0.25).

fig4a-fluovolt-cathodic-decline¶

FluoVolt cathodic polarization fell from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.

def fig4a_decline(mapping, reading="experiment"):
    t = imp_vs_impc("FV", mapping, reading)
    c = t[t.pole == "cath"].set_index("level").dF
    r = dict(cath_360=c.get(360, np.nan), ok_360=bool(abs(c[360] - 71) <= 10) if 360 in c.index else None)
    for L in (1000, 1200, 1400):
        r[f"cath_{L}"] = c.get(L, np.nan)
        r[f"ok_{L}"] = bool(40.5 <= c[L] <= 55) if L in c.index else None
    r["reproduced"] = verdict(r["ok_360"], r["ok_1000"], r["ok_1200"], r["ok_1400"])
    return r

Di-8-ANEPPS claims at 570 V/cm and above¶

Under the adopted top mapping the sets reach 1400 V/cm. The paper's 43 V/cm level has no set, and 1200 V/cm is the 200 V set (1120 V/cm). Under the bottom variant the sets end at 430 V/cm and these criteria cannot be tested; its values at the levels present are shown where they exist. Pole dF at all 19 sets is in the data check.

def fig2b_climbs(mapping, reading="experiment", background=True):
    t = show_levels("Di8", ["pi_cath", "pi_anod"], background, readings=[reading], mappings=[mapping]).set_index("level").sort_index()
    t = t[t.index <= 570]
    steps = {pole: np.diff(np.abs(t[f"pi_{pole}"].values)) for pole in ["cath", "anod"]}
    up = bool(all((s > 0).all() for s in steps.values()))
    return dict(levels=",".join(map(str, t.index)), has_43=43 in t.index, has_570=570 in t.index,
                cath=" ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in t.pi_cath), anod=" ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in t.pi_anod),
                every_step_up=up, reproduced=verdict(up, True if 570 in t.index else None))

Result: partially reproduced (under the assumed factor). Under the top mapping, with experiment means, both poles rise at every step from 150 to 570 V/cm (cathodic -1.6, 2.7, 6.6, 13.0%; anodic -6.2, -7.7, -10.6, -16.7%), and so they do over all cells and without background subtraction. In the sweep the criterion holds at every factor from 2 to 8 V/cm per volt; below 2 there is no 570 V/cm set.

def fig2b_decline_rows(mapping, reading, mode):
    q = stability("Di8", "pulse", mapping, reading, mode)
    q = q[q.level >= 780].copy()
    q["abs_start"], q["abs_end"] = q.start.abs(), q.end.abs()
    q["end_below_start"] = q.abs_end < q.abs_start
    return q

def fig2b_decline(mapping, reading="experiment", mode="b", poles=("cath",)):
    q = fig2b_decline_rows(mapping, reading, mode)
    q = q[q.pole.isin(poles)]
    return dict(n_sets=q.level.nunique(), reproduced=bool(q.end_below_start.all()) if q.level.nunique() == 4 else None)

# Control for drift: the same start-to-end change in every set, split into the offset shared by
# both poles ((cath + anod) / 2) and the polarization amplitude ((cath - anod) / 2). Top mapping,
# experiment means, first 10 against last 10 pulse images.
df = D[D.dye == "Di8"].copy()
for pole in ["cath", "anod"]:
    se = np.array([start_end(f, pef.N_BASE, 100, "b") for f in df[f"frames_{pole}"]])
    df[f"s_{pole}"], df[f"e_{pole}"] = se[:, 0], se[:, 1]
u = units(df, "experiment")
u["d_cath"] = u.e_cath.abs() - u.s_cath.abs()
u["d_anod"] = u.e_anod.abs() - u.s_anod.abs()
u["d_shared"] = (u.e_cath + u.e_anod) / 2 - (u.s_cath + u.s_anod) / 2
u["d_polar"] = (u.e_cath - u.e_anod) / 2 - (u.s_cath - u.s_anod) / 2
drift = u.groupby("volt")[["d_cath", "d_anod", "d_shared", "d_polar"]].mean()
drift.insert(0, "V/cm top", (drift.index * K["top"]).round())
drift["p_cath"] = [stats.ttest_1samp(g.d_cath, 0).pvalue for _, g in u.groupby("volt")]

Result: reproduced (under the assumed factor and pole). Under the top mapping the cathodic |dF| at the end of the pulse images is below the start in every set from 780 V/cm, under every cell reading and both windows. With experiment means and 10-image windows it goes from 19.8 to 17.1, 22.2 to 19.7, 24.4 to 20.8 and 27.0 to 22.4% (p = 0.034, 0.069, 0.037, 0.142). The anodic pole does not decline in any of these sets with experiment means and 10-image windows, and in at most one set under the other readings, so reading (d), both poles, fails. Reading (c), the cathodic pole, is adopted. The text does not name the pole, and the paper places the damage at the cathodic pole (Results 3.1, the cathodic pole dims at 780 V/cm; Results 3.4, the reduction is more pronounced at the cathodic pole). The drift control limits what this shows. Below 780 V/cm the cathodic |dF| also falls within the set in 9 of 11 sets (mean -1.76%). From 780 V/cm it falls by -3.32% on average, of which the offset shared by both poles is -2.15% and the polarization amplitude -1.17%. Most of the decline is a drift present at every field strength, and the part specific to strong fields is small.

fig4b-di8-limits¶

With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, measured IMP fell below the calculated value at 570 V/cm, where dF peaked at 57 +- 14% (cathodic) and -55 +- 4% (anodic), over 600 mV.

In [27]:
def fig4b_limits(mapping, reading="experiment", tests=("p_paired", "p_unpaired")):
    t = imp_vs_impc("Di8", mapping, reading)
    r = limits_check(t, "Di8", 57, 14, -55, 4)
    r["peaks_at_570"] = bool(r["at"] == 570 and r["at_a"] == 570) if 570 in t.level.values else None
    for test in tests:
        at570 = t[t.level == 570]
        r[f"{test}_below_at_570"] = bool(((at570[test] < 0.05) & (at570.imp.abs() < at570.impc.abs())).any()) if len(at570) else None
        low = t[t.level <= 360]
        r[f"{test}_not_below_43_360"] = bool(not ((low[test] < 0.05) & (low.imp.abs() < low.impc.abs())).any())
        r[f"reproduced_{test}"] = verdict(r["max_cath_ok"], r["min_anod_ok"], r["peaks_at_570"], r[f"{test}_below_at_570"], r[f"{test}_not_below_43_360"])
    return r

fig4b-first-10-pulses¶

Averaged over only the first 10 of the 60 pulses, Di-8-ANEPPS cathodic polarization reached 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), so the 600-mV maximum is not the dye's limit.

In [28]:
def fig4b_first10(mapping, reading="experiment"):
    t = show_levels("Di8", ["f10_cath", "dF_cath"], readings=[reading], mappings=[mapping]).set_index("level")
    ok = bool(abs(t.f10_cath.max() - 66) <= 15)
    return dict(max_first10=t.f10_cath.max(), at=int(t.f10_cath.idxmax()), within_66_15=ok, max_60=t.dF_cath.max(),
                above_60_max=bool(t.f10_cath.max() > t.dF_cath.max()), reproduced=verdict(ok, bool(t.f10_cath.max() > t.dF_cath.max())))

fig4b-cathodic-asymmetry¶

Above 780 V/cm the pole IMP fell progressively with field strength, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm the cathodic pole no longer charged and the anodic pole fell to about -30% dF.

In [29]:
def fig4b_asym(mapping, reading="experiment"):
    u = units(D[D.dye == "Di8"], reading)
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(u.volt, K[mapping])
    if not all(L in lv for L in (780, 1000, 1200, 1400)):
        return dict(reproduced=None)
    m = {L: u[u.volt == lv[L]] for L in (780, 1000, 1200, 1400)}
    c = {L: g.dF_cath.mean() for L, g in m.items()}
    a = {L: g.dF_anod.mean() for L, g in m.items()}
    dec = all(abs(c[L]) < abs(c[780]) for L in (1000, 1200, 1400)) and all(abs(a[L]) < abs(a[780]) for L in (1000, 1200, 1400))
    lost_c = 1 - abs(c[1400]) / abs(c[780])
    lost_a = 1 - abs(a[1400]) / abs(a[780])
    t1 = stats.ttest_1samp(m[1400].dF_cath, 0)
    r = dict(cath=" ".join(f"{c[L]:.1f}" for L in (780, 1000, 1200, 1400)), anod=" ".join(f"{a[L]:.1f}" for L in (780, 1000, 1200, 1400)),
             decreases=dec, lost_cath=lost_c, lost_anod=lost_a, more_at_cath=lost_c > lost_a, cath_1400=c[1400],
             p_cath_1400_vs_0=t1.pvalue, anod_1400=a[1400], anod_ok=bool(abs(a[1400] + 30) <= 3))
    r["reproduced"] = verdict(bool(dec), bool(lost_c > lost_a), bool(t1.pvalue >= 0.05), r["anod_ok"])
    return r

Under the top mapping both poles keep growing from 780 to 1400 V/cm (cathodic 18.1, 20.4, 22.5, 24.3%; anodic -21.2, -25.7, -27.8, -29.2%, experiment means), so condition (1) fails under every cell reading. fig4c-equator-follows-cosine¶

Membrane regions nearer the equator were unaffected by pole electroporation and followed the cosine dependence of the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm.

Measured IMP (dF / 9.1%) against IMPC, averaged per unit within arcs beside the two equator points (90 and 270 degrees from the cathode), (a) 15 and (b) 30 degrees wide, on the cathodic and anodic side of each; 2-tailed paired t-test at 570, 780 and 1000 V/cm.

In [30]:
def equator_arcs(width):
    th = np.arange(360)
    return {"90_cath_side": (th >= 90 - width) & (th < 90), "90_anod_side": (th > 90) & (th <= 90 + width),
            "270_anod_side": (th >= 270 - width) & (th < 270), "270_cath_side": (th > 270) & (th <= 270 + width)}

def fig4c_rows(mapping, reading, width):
    df = D[D.dye == "Di8"]
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(df.volt, K[mapping])
    rows = []
    for L in (570, 780, 1000):
        if L not in lv:
            continue
        g = df[df.volt == lv[L]]
        for name, sel in equator_arcs(width).items():
            meas = np.array([p[sel].mean() for p in g.profile]) / pef.SENS["Di8"] * 100
            calc = np.array([pef.impc_mV(lv[L] * K[mapping], r, np.arange(360))[sel].mean() for r in g.R_area_um])
            x = g.assign(meas=meas, calc=calc)
            x = units(x, reading) if reading != "experiment" else x.groupby("subject", as_index=False)[["meas", "calc"]].mean()
            p = stats.ttest_rel(x.meas, x.calc).pvalue
            rows.append(dict(cells=reading, width=width, level=L, arc=name, n=len(x), meas=x.meas.mean(), calc=x.calc.mean(),
                             ratio=x.meas.mean() / x.calc.mean(), p=p, differs=p < 0.05))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def fig4c(mapping, reading="experiment", width=15):
    t = fig4c_rows(mapping, reading, width)
    if t.empty or t.level.nunique() < 3:
        return dict(n_differ=int(t.differs.sum()) if len(t) else 0, reproduced=verdict(False) if len(t) and t.differs.any() else None)
    return dict(n_differ=int(t.differs.sum()), n_tests=len(t), reproduced=not bool(t.differs.any()))

eq = pd.concat([fig4c_rows("top", reading, width) for reading in READINGS for width in (15, 30)])

fig1-pole-dimming¶

With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.

(1) The mean cathodic pole dF at 780 V/cm is not above that at 570 V/cm; (2) at 1400 V/cm the largest mean dF of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies outside the +-5 degree polar arc. Backgrounds (a) and (b).

In [31]:
def fig1(mapping, reading="experiment", df0=None):
    df0 = D if df0 is None else df0
    u = units(df0[df0.dye == "Di8"], reading)
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(u.volt, K[mapping])
    if not all(L in lv for L in (570, 780, 1400)):
        return dict(reproduced=None)
    c570 = u[u.volt == lv[570]].dF_cath.mean()
    c780 = u[u.volt == lv[780]].dF_cath.mean()
    g14 = units(df0[(df0.dye == "Di8") & (df0.volt == lv[1400])], "centre" if reading == "centre" else "cells")
    if reading == "experiment":
        prof = np.mean([np.mean(np.stack(g.profile.values), 0) for _, g in g14.groupby("subject")], 0)
    else:
        prof = np.mean(np.stack(g14.profile.values), 0)
    hemi = np.r_[np.arange(270, 360), np.arange(0, 91)]
    peak = hemi[np.argmax(prof[hemi])]
    off = (peak + 180) % 360 - 180
    return dict(cath_570=c570, cath_780=c780, cond1=bool(c780 <= c570), peak_deg_from_cathode=off, peak_dF=prof[peak],
                pole_dF=pef.arc(prof, 0), cond2=bool(abs(off) > 5), reproduced=verdict(bool(c780 <= c570), bool(abs(off) > 5)))

Result: not reproduced (under the assumed factor). Under the top mapping the mean cathodic dF at 780 V/cm (18.1%) is above that at 570 V/cm (13.0%), so condition (1) fails under every cell and background reading (10.6 against 12.1% for the cell nearest the centre; 7.4 against 9.9% without background). At 1400 V/cm the peak of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies 12 to 46 degrees from the pole, so condition (2) holds. No factor from 5 to 8 meets the criterion; below 5 there is no 1400 V/cm set.

fig7b-charging-during-pulse¶

Normalized to 150 V/cm, pole polarization during the conditioning pulse fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm, and further at stronger fields (p < 0.01 for every point from 560 V/cm).

Collapsed pole dF as % of the 150 V/cm value, against the line 100% x E / 150. Normalization (a) per cell, (b) of the means; pole (c) each, (d) mean of the poles. One-sample t-test of the per-unit values against the line.

In [32]:
def fig7b_rows(mapping, reading):
    u = units(D[D.dye == "Di8"], reading)
    lv = pef.nearest_sets(u.volt, K[mapping])
    if not all(L in lv for L in (150, 570, 780, 1000, 1200, 1400)):
        return pd.DataFrame()
    base = u[u.volt == lv[150]].set_index("unit")
    rows = []
    for pole in ["cath", "anod", "mean"]:
        def val(g):
            return (g.dF_cath - g.dF_anod) / 2 if pole == "mean" else g[f"dF_{pole}"].abs()
        b = val(base)
        r = dict(mapping=mapping, cells=reading, pole=pole)
        okp = True
        for L in (570, 780, 1000, 1200, 1400):
            g = u[u.volt == lv[L]].set_index("unit")
            line = 100 * lv[L] / lv[150]
            pc = 100 * val(g) / b
            r[f"ratio_a_{L}"] = line / pc.mean()
            r[f"ratio_b_{L}"] = line / (100 * val(g).mean() / b.mean())
            p = stats.ttest_1samp(pc, line).pvalue
            r[f"p_{L}"] = p
            okp &= bool(p < 0.01 and pc.mean() < line)
        r["all_below_p01"] = okp
        for nm in ("a", "b"):
            r[f"ok_{nm}"] = bool(abs(r[f"ratio_{nm}_570"] - 1.5) <= 0.15 and abs(r[f"ratio_{nm}_780"] - 2) <= 0.2
                                 and all(r[f"ratio_{nm}_{L}"] > 2 for L in (1000, 1200, 1400)) and okp)
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def fig7b(mapping, reading="experiment"):
    t = fig7b_rows(mapping, reading)
    return dict(reproduced=bool((t.ok_a | t.ok_b).any()) if len(t) else None)

f7 = pd.concat([fig7b_rows("top", reading) for reading in READINGS])
print("Top mapping (560 V/cm is the 100 V set, 760 V/cm the 140 V set at 784 V/cm):")
print(f7.round(3).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced (under the assumed factor). Under the top mapping, normalized to the 150 V/cm set (25 V), no reading meets the criterion. At 25 V both poles share a bleaching offset (mean of the poles -3.9% in Di-8-ANEPPS, data check), which makes the anodic |dF| at 150 V/cm too large and the cathodic one too small, and so biases the anodic ratios up and the cathodic ones down. The anodic pole with experiment means gives linear-over-measured ratios of 1.46 at 560 V/cm (within 1.5 +- 0.15) and 1.62 at 760 V/cm (outside 2 +- 0.2), and 1.72, 1.76 and 2.08 at 1000 to 1400 V/cm, so it exceeds 2 only at 1400. Every datapoint of that reading is below the line at p < 0.01. Its values are nearest the paper's, but it is the reading the offset affects most. The cathodic ratios are 0.63 to 0.94 with experiment means. The mean of the poles, in which the offset cancels, gives 0.55 to 0.85 with experiment means, so the measured polarization lies above the linear line at every level. With per-cell normalization over all cells or for the centre cell, the mean of the poles gives ratios such as -10.7 and 16.9, because the 150 V/cm values are near zero there; those ratios carry no information. In the sweep only 5.6 and 6.25 V/cm per volt have every level, and neither meets the criterion.

fig5b-conductivity-calibration¶

By Eq. (2), the effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold rise reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold rise by 12%.

Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 (lambda_i 0.4 S/m, lambda_o 1.64 S/m, R 8 um, d 5 nm, intact lambda_m 3e-7 S/m); no recordings. Reduction read as (a) 1 - f/1.5 and (b) 1 - f(lambda_m) / f(3e-7 S/m).

In [33]:

    rows.append(dict(fold=fold, lambda_m=3e-7 * fold, f=f, reduction_a=100 * (1 - f / 1.5), reduction_b=100 * (1 - f / f0)))

Result: partially reproduced. Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives f = 1.498 for the intact membrane. A 10-fold rise in conductivity reduces IMP by 1.33% under reading (a) and 1.20% under (b), against 2 +- 0.2; it takes a 15.2-fold rise to reach 2%. A 100-fold rise reduces IMP by 11.87% and 11.75%, within 12 +- 1.2. The claim's qualitative point holds: the reduction stays small until the conductivity rises more than 30-fold (3.9% at 30-fold).

Outcomes across the factor from volts to V/cm¶

The factor is not recorded, so each criterion is run over factors from 1.5 to 8 V/cm per volt: the two endpoint readings (1.72 and 5.6), the two-dimensional rod estimates for the paper's geometry (4.64 and 7.19, data check) and steps between. Sets are named by the paper's levels as elsewhere (nearest within 15%). Each criterion is run on its adopted reading: experiment means, background subtracted, 10-image windows, the paired test, the cathodic pole for fig2b-di8-decline-within-set, and every smooth for fig3-fluovolt-nonlinear. "yes" is reproduced, "no" not reproduced, "-" a level the criterion needs has no set at that factor.

def sweep(DD):
    # Every criterion at every factor, on the pole table DD (the criterion functions read the global D).
    global D
    D_main = D
    D = DD
    try:
        return pd.DataFrame([sweep_row(k) for k in SWEEP]).set_index("factor")
    finally:
        D = D_main

With the peak trace, no factor run from 1.5 to 8 reproduces fig3-dye-sensitivity (nor any on the finer grid from 1.40 to 2.30 in its section), fig3-fluovolt-nonlinear, the FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS maxima (fig2a-fluovolt-saturation, fig4a-fluovolt-limits, fig4a-fluovolt-cathodic-decline, fig4b-di8-limits, fig4b-first-10-pulses), fig4b-cathodic-asymmetry, fig4c-equator-follows-cosine, fig1-pole-dimming or fig7b-charging-during-pulse. fig2b-di8-climbs-to-570 holds at every factor from 2 to 8, fig2b-di8-decline-within-set at every factor from 5.6 to 8 (below 5.6 there is no 1400 V/cm set), and fig2a-fluovolt-stable only at 3.5. At the geometric factors (4.64 to 7.19) the slopes are 4.4 to 8.0 (FluoVolt) and 1.6 to 3.2 (Di-8-ANEPPS). With the edge trace the results differ only for fig2a-fluovolt-stable (met at 8, not at 3.5) and fig4c-equator-follows-cosine at 2 (tested and not met). At the adopted 5.6, every result is the same under both traces.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • The files give the pulse in volts. The factor to V/cm is taken as 5.6 V/cm per volt (1400 V/cm at 250 V). This is an assumption, supported by the electrode geometry of Methods 2.2 (4.64 to 7.19 in a two-dimensional model). The bottom reading (1.72) is shown as a variant, and every criterion is run over factors from 1.5 to 8. Sets are named by the paper's level nearest them. The sweep separates two kinds of failure. The FluoVolt and Di-8-ANEPPS maxima fail at every factor. Only fig2b-di8-climbs-to-570 (2 to 8), fig2b-di8-decline-within-set (5.6 to 8) and fig2a-fluovolt-stable (3.5 only) hold at some factors.
  • The paper analysed one cell per experiment; the files show 3 to 6 cells per field and do not say which. Experiment means, the cell nearest the image centre, and all cells are each run.
  • Membrane traces are found automatically, not drawn by hand. The peak trace is drawn inwards in some cells, and one object in c7 is two touching cells. Moving the trace within 3 pixels, or following the cell edge, does not bring the mean pole dF near the paper's values, and at the adopted factor the edge trace changes no result. Dark frames are left out, so most baselines have 39 images. The pixel size (0.267 um) is assumed from the camera and objective, and tau is from reference [20].
  • The mean of per-image pole dF and the collapsed-image pole dF are the same number here, because both use the same baseline mean as F0, so the Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 measures coincide.

What was found about the dataset:

  • It holds ten 19-set escalations of 1-us pulses (25 to 250 V), five per dye, from one day. It holds none of the paper's alternating, 0.3-us, Gd3+, Ca2+ or two-pulse experiments. Its voltages span a factor of 10, so no single factor maps them onto the paper's 43 to 1400 V/cm series.
  • The files state an electrode distance of 1.00 mm; the paper states 1.6 mm. They give no field strength, field direction, pixel size or cell identity. The field direction is clear from the data (cathode-facing side towards the bottom of the image in every experiment).
  • Frame 0 is dark in 175 of 190 sets, and 51 other frames are dark, which the files do not mention.
  • No recording is deposited twice.
